emails.subject: New FIX session to the dark pool venue - UAT plan and cutover
emails.body:
Hi Daniel, Sam,

Quick update on the new FIX 4.4 connection to the alternative trading venue we scoped last month. The venue's certification environment is now live and Travis and I ran the first set of test orders through OMS this morning. New order single, cancel/replace and cancel all acked cleanly, and execution reports map correctly into TradeBlotter, including the last-liquidity indicator.

Open items before we go live:
1. Sequence number reset behavior on reconnect needs confirming with the venue's support desk.
2. We need Sam's team to whitelist the venue's gateway addresses on the egress firewall for production.
3. Min-quantity and IOC handling should be signed off by the desk before we enable smart-order routing to it.

My proposal is to complete certification this week, run a one-day pilot with capped order sizes on Monday 2026-07-13, and then open it up to routing if fills look clean. Please let me know if that timing works.

Thanks,
Steven

emails.subject: Trade error write-up - duplicate child orders on 2026-07-16
emails.body:
Daniel, Marcus,

Below is the write-up for the trade error that occurred yesterday, Thursday 2026-07-16, on the mid-cap sell program.

What happened: Around 14:22 ET a parent order was resubmitted from OMS after a UI timeout. The original was actually accepted, so two sets of child orders worked in the market. The result was an over-sell of roughly 18,000 shares against the intended 60,000 before the duplicate was spotted at 14:31 and cancelled.

Impact: The desk went short for about 40 minutes and bought back the excess at a loss of approximately $9,400. The loss was booked to the error account and is visible in TradeBlotter.

Root cause: No duplicate-order check on resubmission and I did not confirm the order status before resending.

Actions: I will confirm status in the order audit trail before any resend, and I have asked for a client-order-id duplicate warning in OMS. Owen, a note for the risk log is attached to the ticket.

Happy to walk through it on Monday.

Regards,
Travis

emails.subject: Broker commission review - Q2 results and proposed tier changes
emails.body:
Hi Daniel,

I finished the broker commission review for Q2 and wanted to share the main findings before our vendor meeting.

We paid roughly $1.84M in commissions across eleven brokers. Three brokers account for about 58% of the spend, but their research scores from the desk are middling. Meanwhile two smaller brokers delivered strong algo execution, with implementation shortfall roughly 4 bps better than the pool average, yet received under 6% of flow.

Recommendations:
1. Shift about 10% of the flow from the bottom-scoring large broker to the two high-performing smaller ones.
2. Renegotiate the cash equity rate on high-touch from 3.0 cents to 2.5 cents for the top tier given our volume.
3. Review the soft-dollar allocation, since several research payments look unused.

Jonathan has the underlying data cut from TradeBlotter if you want to check the numbers. I would like to finalize by mid-September.

Thanks,
Jessica

emails.subject: Follow-up on the sector concentration limit breach from 2026-09-04
emails.body:
Owen, Paul,

Following up on the sector concentration limit breach last Friday. The desk's financials exposure reached 112% of the intraday limit between 11:05 and 13:40 ET, driven by Erik's accumulation ahead of the index rebalance. The pre-trade check in OMS warned but allowed the orders under the override flag.

What we have done:
1. Erik reduced the position back under 90% of limit by close, and I reviewed the blotter fills.
2. The override flag is now restricted to myself and the desk heads.
3. We agreed to add a soft alert at 85% so the desk gets earlier notice.

What I need from Risk: confirmation that the RiskEngine exposure feed reflected the position correctly during the window, since the numbers I saw in TradeBlotter lagged by a few minutes. Marcus, copying you for the compliance record.

Can we meet Friday to close this out?

Thanks,
Daniel

emails.subject: Trade error write-up - wrong side on ETF hedge order 2026-10-13
emails.body:
Daniel, Owen,

Writing up yesterday's error, Tuesday 2026-10-13.

Summary: At about 10:47 ET I entered an ETF hedge order for the energy book as a buy instead of a sell. 25,000 shares were executed at the market before I caught the mistake at 10:52, when the position on TradeBlotter looked wrong. I reversed it immediately and then placed the correct order.

Impact: The cost was roughly $6,200 from the spread and adverse move, charged to the error account. There was no client impact, and no limit was breached.

Cause: I was working fast during a volatile open, and the OMS ticket defaulted to the side from my previous order. The confirmation screen did not highlight the side.

Follow-up: I will slow down on hedge entries and read back side and quantity. I also suggest that OMS color-code buy and sell on the confirmation step. Steven has offered to pair on a quick checklist for the desk.

Apologies for the noise.

Erik
